submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective lexical detector for tokens from outside the ordinary English core: it peaks on the fragment that completes a multi-token proper noun or specialist/technical term ('istan' in Uzbek[istan]/Turkmen[istan]/Afghan[istan] ~1.0-1.2 of max, 'if' in sans-ser[if] ~1.3, 'isp' in B[isp]henol, 'aic' in Aram[aic], 'iazep' in benzod[iazep]ine, 'op' in had[op]) and on whole rare proper/technical nouns (Iraq, Afghanistan, Asia, Africa, wheat, grain, domain, deficit), plus, more diffusely, byte fragments of non-Latin scripts (Devanagari, Arabic, CJK pieces). It stays at or below zero on high-frequency function words and on the ordinary English core vocabulary (the, of, country, city, table, water, plan, meeting), on rare-but-mundane general words (xylophone, quixotic, clandestine), and on the commonest Western country names (France, Germany, Spain, Sweden read ~0 while Iraq, Iran, Syria, Korea read 0.7-1.3); a weaker background response to a few common abstract nouns (' thing' up to 1.0, ' event', ' rate', ' whatever' ~0.3-0.6) is the acknowledged leftover.
